title: Semantic token layer with complete dark and light palettes
asA: user who prefers a dark interface
iWant: a dark theme that is as considered and complete as the light one
soThat: choosing dark mode never costs me legibility or polish

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every colour declaration in component styles resolves to a semantic token (surface, on-surface, primary, on-primary, accent, danger, warning, success, muted, or their declared derivatives); raw hex or rgb values do not appear in component styles.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every colour routes through a semantic token

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every semantic token declared for the light theme has a declared dark value; parity is verified over the token file, and a missing pair fails the build.
acceptanceCriteria.given: assets/tokens/design-tokens.json as integrated into the project
acceptanceCriteria.when: the token sets are diffed by key
acceptanceCriteria.then: the light and dark key sets are identical

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every token pairing used for text or essential UI meets the contrast thresholds in both themes: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text and non-text UI.
acceptanceCriteria.when: contrast is computed for both themes
acceptanceCriteria.then: every pairing meets its threshold in light and in dark

acceptanceCriteria.description: First visit with no stored preference follows prefers-color-scheme.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh browser profile with a dark OS preference
acceptanceCriteria.then: the dark theme renders without a flash of the wrong theme

acceptanceCriteria.description: Elevation, borders, and disabled states remain distinguishable in dark mode; dark is not a naive inversion that flattens hierarchy.
acceptanceCriteria.given: components with elevation and disabled states
acceptanceCriteria.then: surface levels and disabled affordances are visually distinct per the token definitions
